name: claude-motion-design (Howseen)
one_line: Skill that builds a film as one seek(t) HTML page, captures it frame by frame, and cuts to the beat.
best_for: Beat-synced launch films with zero framework licence questions
license_notes: MIT covers the code. The example's fetch_assets.py pulls Mixkit/Pexels/Unsplash media and brand logos that keep their own terms.
install_risk: Medium-low. pip installs Playwright/numpy/Pillow and downloads Chromium. Optional helper reads a 21st.dev API key from env or ~/.config/21st.key and calls their MCP endpoint; asset/logo search scripts hit the network.
reason: Closest match to the kit's exact pipeline (HTML + Playwright + ffmpeg), deterministic, no Remotion or GSAP dependency.

name: Motion Graphics Skill Pack (charlie947)
one_line: Fifteen focused skills for launch videos, animated charts and reels, starting from a brand-intake step.
best_for: A ready set of launch-film workflows split into small single-purpose skills
license_notes: Plain MIT; author asks (does not require) a link back.
install_risk: Low. Repo is Markdown skills plus one validation shell script; README states no API key is needed. Installing via `npx skills` sends anonymous telemetry (see vercel-labs/skills) unless disabled; manual copy avoids that.
reason: Clean licence, small surface, launch-video focus, actively updated (pushed 2026-10-11).

name: Animate (cth9191)
one_line: Procedural single-canvas animations in seven built-in looks, with story/look/storyboard approval gates before rendering.
best_for: Illustrated explainers and product reels in a distinctive drawn style
license_notes: MIT. Uses local system fonts, so no font files are redistributed.
install_risk: Low-medium. Needs Node, Playwright Chromium and ffmpeg. Voice-over path optionally calls the ElevenLabs connector and runs faster-whisper locally (model download).
reason: Strong cheap-preview gating, deterministic canvas output, nothing paid on the default path.

name: product-launch-motion
one_line: Directs and renders a launch film from HTML, CSS and GSAP, including grade and a two-pass loudness master.
best_for: End-to-end product launch films with voice-over and broadcast-level audio
license_notes: MIT covers authored text and scripts only. NOTICE says the reference film and its still belong to Cheerful and are not licensed. GSAP's own standard licence applies.
install_risk: Low. Bash/Node scripts call ffmpeg locally (master.sh reviewed: measure, limit, re-encode). README vendors GSAP by downloading the file with curl (not piped to a shell). Voice is optional: ElevenLabs (paid) or local Kokoro.
reason: Most complete launch-film craft guide among the seeds; clear notice about what the licence does not cover.

name: hyperframes-motion-reel
one_line: Turns a one-line theme into a beat-locked HyperFrames showreel with GSAP choreography and seekable canvas layers.
best_for: Fast, energetic sizzle reels and brand teasers
license_notes: MIT. Built to avoid Remotion's company licence; still depends on GSAP (Webflow standard licence).
install_risk: Low. Skill content is Markdown; the only code is a VitePress docs site. HyperFrames CLI downloads its own headless Chrome.
reason: Small, readable, licence-conscious port of a Remotion workflow to Apache-2.0 tooling.

name: claude-motion
one_line: Taste rules, a stdlib Python sound synth, frame self-review, plus a three.js web-sim capture pipeline.
best_for: Simulation-style pieces and synthesized sound without sample licensing
license_notes: MIT for the repo. The main composition path is Remotion, so Remotion's company licence applies to larger companies; the sims/ path avoids it.
install_risk: Medium. npm install + Playwright Chromium download. Example MCP config runs `npx -y ...@latest` and `uvx` servers and asks for an ElevenLabs key; Figma MCP is remote. All optional, but `@latest` pins nothing.
reason: Excellent ideas (pure-function render(t), synthesized SFX); Remotion dependency and unpinned MCP examples need care.

name: claude-remotion-skill
one_line: Remotion skill encoding easing, staggering, grading and render-then-inspect rules for motion graphics.
best_for: Teams already on Remotion who want better default motion
license_notes: Skill is MIT; Remotion itself requires a paid company licence for for-profit orgs above 3 people.
install_risk: Low. Markdown skill plus example project; example scripts synthesize SFX and a music bed locally. Normal npm install of Remotion.
reason: Good craft rules, but output depends on Remotion licensing.

name: Klik Motion-Graphics System
one_line: Three Remotion skills: element animation laws, camera grammar, and a storyboard-first production method.
best_for: Reading for camera and choreography vocabulary
license_notes: No LICENSE file and GitHub reports none, so all rights are reserved by default. Also sits on Remotion's licence.
install_risk: Medium. Ships prebuilt .skill/.zip bundles in dist/ whose contents cannot be diffed against source at a glance; Python/Node helper scripts; README warns of heavy token use.
reason: No licence means you cannot legally redistribute or adapt it; prebuilt bundles add review burden.

name: motion-design-skills (iart.ai)
one_line: Nine skills on timing, colour, composition, After Effects, Remotion, logo stings and backgrounds.
best_for: Fundamentals reference that is renderer-agnostic
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. Markdown plus three ffprobe/ffmpeg helper shell scripts. README funnels to the vendor's hosted agent with tracking parameters.
reason: Decent fundamentals, but partly a marketing funnel and not updated since June 2026.

name: HyperFrames Student Kit
one_line: Fifteen skills for cutting footage, captions, storytelling and HyperFrames motion graphics, mirrored for Claude and Codex.
best_for: Editing talking-head footage into reels with motion overlays
license_notes: MIT for original kit; imported pipeline resources use a custom 'use permission' grant; GSAP and fonts keep their own licences; example media and brand references grant no rights.
install_risk: Medium. Large repo (1,000+ files, 80+ scripts). Transcription helper calls ElevenLabs Scribe; showreel scripts call Kie.ai for generated assets (both paid, optional). Node 22+, Playwright.
reason: Useful but aimed at footage editing and leans on paid services; mixed licence grants.

name: Remotion Agent Skills (official)
one_line: Official Remotion skills covering project creation, markup, captions, rendering, maps and upgrades.
best_for: Correct, current Remotion API usage
license_notes: This mirror has no LICENSE file; it is synced from the Remotion monorepo, which uses the source-available Remotion License (company licence for for-profits with 4+ people, contractors count in 5.0).
install_risk: Low. Markdown skills; map techniques reference MapTiler/Cesium, which need their own API tokens.
reason: Authoritative for Remotion, but licence is inherited and not stated in the repo.

name: Motion Design Skill (LottieFiles)
one_line: Tool-agnostic motion direction: timing, easing tables, choreography and Disney principles adapted for screens.
best_for: Raising the motion taste of any other skill or engine
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Very low. Pure Markdown, no scripts.
reason: Zero-risk, engine-independent principles; pairs with any renderer.

name: motion-graphics (Barty-Bart)
one_line: Six single-job skills: B-roll synced to words, subject cutouts, product explainers and a CC0 sound pass.
best_for: Adding motion B-roll and sound design to existing footage
license_notes: MIT; GitHub shows NOASSERTION only because the file appends notes. Geist fonts OFL-1.1, icon paths from Lucide (ISC), bundled SFX CC0.
install_risk: Medium. setup.sh installs Playwright + Chromium into ./motion and, if numpy is missing, falls back to `pip install --break-system-packages`. Sound skill installs librosa into a local folder; cutout skill downloads a local ML model.
reason: Well-scoped and CC0 audio, but setup can touch the system Python; README upsells a paid community.

name: Motion.dev Animations Skill
one_line: Teaches the agent Motion.dev patterns for springs, scroll effects and reduced-motion handling in web apps.
best_for: Website and UI animation, not rendered video
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. Markdown plus one Python config validator.
reason: Fine for site motion; off-target for frame-captured films and quiet since March 2026.

name: GSAP AI Skills (official)
one_line: Official GreenSock skills for timelines, tweens, ScrollTrigger, plugins and framework integration.
best_for: Making the agent write correct, seekable GSAP timelines
license_notes: Skills are MIT. GSAP itself is under Webflow's standard no-charge licence, not an OSI licence.
install_risk: Low. Markdown skills.
reason: Official and current; most HTML launch-film skills use GSAP timelines.

name: anidoodle
one_line: Hand-drawn art in 32 media styles, with drawing-timelapse films and a written score, all generated as code.
best_for: Illustrated, crafted-looking launch films and explainers
license_notes: Apache-2.0, copyright Alex Greenshpun.
install_risk: Medium-low. Installed via plugin marketplace. Optional sound pack is downloaded by a soundfetch tool (sampled instruments).
reason: Distinctive look, permissive licence, deterministic output.

name: motionmaxxing
one_line: Measured before/after protocol that pushes generic AI motion toward designed films, on HyperFrames.
best_for: A critique-and-upgrade pass over a draft film
license_notes: Apache-2.0 with NOTICE. Bundles GSAP 3.12.5, three.js, opentype.js and Inter under their own licences.
install_risk: Medium. install.sh checks requirements and links/copies the skill. Optional ElevenLabs key for voice/SFX/music; optional Codex CLI image generation. Author calls it an early release.
reason: Good QA ideas; early and tied to optional paid audio.

name: no-slop-motion
one_line: Ten-gate process and banned-cliché list for launch and brand films that feel directed.
best_for: Script, voice and art-direction discipline for brand films
license_notes: MIT; bundled fonts OFL-1.1.
install_risk: Medium-low. Python requirements for audio and render scripts. Voice step expects a Cartesia API key; music via Suno or a licensed track.
reason: Strong anti-cliché rules; full pipeline assumes paid TTS.

name: Motion Video Kit
one_line: Critic-loop skill for business commercials: motion grammar, 28 analysed launch films, Three.js product patterns, QA checks.
best_for: Quality review loop and product-hero 3D shots
license_notes: MIT. Reference films are linked, not redistributed.
install_risk: Low. Markdown plus ffmpeg/ffprobe measurement scripts; HyperFrames optional.
reason: Renderer-agnostic, measurable QA, honest about AI imagery.

name: saas-motion-kit
one_line: HyperFrames kit for software promos with 101 themes, a transition atlas and a repetition audit.
best_for: Varied SaaS promo films that avoid template sameness
license_notes: MIT; fonts OFL-1.1. README warns MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC, so not for commercial music.
install_risk: Low. Needs Node 22+, ffmpeg; HyperFrames downloads its own Chrome.
reason: Directly on-topic, permissive, well documented.

name: Lemo-Opuscar
one_line: Library of 43 film styles, each with a reusable style prompt and a code-made example short.
best_for: Picking and reusing a visual style for a short film
license_notes: MIT; demo third-party assets keep their own licences (see each demo's CREDITS).
install_risk: Medium. Installed as a Claude Code plugin; its library in ~/lemo-opuscar updates itself on the next run, so code changes arrive without review. Needs Node 20+, ffmpeg, Python 3.11+.
reason: Great style range; self-updating library should be pinned or disabled.

name: huashu-art-motion
one_line: Chinese-language skill animating 35 art styles with 9 explainer grammars and parametric clip templates.
best_for: Painterly and art-history styled motion pieces
license_notes: MIT except: stroke-order data under Arphic Public License, fonts under OFL, and the author's cartoon character art is excluded.
install_risk: Medium-low. Needs uv, ffmpeg, Playwright Chromium. Skill text is Chinese.
reason: Impressive styles; mixed exceptions and language barrier for an English kit.

name: anything2explainer
one_line: Topic-to-narrated-explainer method with a Remotion template, primitives library and TTS tooling.
best_for: Personal or non-commercial explainer videos
license_notes: Toolkit is noncommercial only; commercial use needs the author's permission (videos you make are yours). Also on Remotion's licence; edge-tts voice is a Microsoft cloud call.
install_risk: Medium. brew/apt installs including sudo apt lines, pip installs, local Kokoro model download.
reason: Noncommercial licence makes it unsuitable for brand/launch work.

name: guizang product video skill
one_line: Chinese-language skill that turns a repo's recent changes into a promo using the product's real components.
best_for: Release-note promos that reuse the product's own UI code
license_notes: Main content AGPL-3.0. Default styles adapted from CodePilot stay under Business Source License 1.1 with their own use grant and change date.
install_risk: Medium. First run checks and installs Node/Python/FFmpeg render dependencies.
reason: Smart 'use your real components' idea, but AGPL + BSL mix needs legal reading before reuse.

name: OpenMontage
one_line: Large agentic production system with many pipelines and provider integrations for generated and composed video.
best_for: Teams wanting one system that also orchestrates AI image/video/voice providers
license_notes: AGPL-3.0. Its composer uses Remotion, so Remotion's company licence also applies.
install_risk: High surface. Python venv + npm installs, piper-tts, and a long list of optional paid provider keys (FAL, Kling, Suno, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, xAI, Google...).
reason: Powerful but heavy, copyleft, and mostly about paid generation rather than code-drawn frames.

name: skills CLI (npx skills)
one_line: The installer most skill READMEs use to copy skills into Claude Code and 40+ other agents.
best_for: Installing skills from GitHub repos
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Medium. Anonymous install telemetry is on by default; opt out with DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK. Runs remote content into your skills folder.
reason: Convenient, but disable telemetry and read what it installs; manual copy is equally fine.

name: HyperFrames
one_line: Compose video as HTML with timing data attributes, then render deterministically to MP4 via headless Chrome.
best_for: The default open engine for agent-written launch films
license_notes: Apache-2.0, no per-render or company-size limits. Optional HeyGen cloud render is a hosted service. Many compositions use GSAP, which has its own licence.
install_risk: Medium-low. CLI downloads a headless Chrome; ships agent skills. Optional cloud-render and AWS Lambda deploy paths need accounts.
reason: Purpose-built for agents, permissive, very active, large ecosystem of skills.

name: Remotion
one_line: React components rendered to video frame by frame, with Studio preview and cloud render options.
best_for: React teams that want a mature video framework
license_notes: Source-available, not OSI. Free for individuals, non-profits and for-profits up to 3 employees; others need a paid company licence. In 5.0 contractors count toward team size. Reselling a derivative is forbidden.
install_risk: Medium-low. npm install pulls a bundled Chromium/ffmpeg toolchain; Lambda rendering needs AWS.
reason: Excellent tech, but the company-licence threshold is the biggest trap for brand teams.

name: html-video
one_line: Local HTML-to-MP4 toolkit for coding agents with 21 licence-tagged templates and a gallery.
best_for: Template-driven promos and data clips rendered on a laptop
license_notes: Apache-2.0; each template records its SPDX licence and attribution flags.
install_risk: Medium-low. Headless Chromium + ffmpeg; optional MiniMax API key for soundtrack.
reason: Licence-clean templates and a fully local render path.

name: Motion Canvas
one_line: TypeScript generator-based animation with a live editor, aimed at explainer-style vector motion.
best_for: Explainers with tight code-driven timing and voice sync
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. Standard npm packages. Rendering is driven from its browser editor rather than a headless API.
reason: Lovely API, but headless batch rendering for agents is easier in Revideo or HyperFrames.

name: Revideo
one_line: Motion Canvas fork with a headless renderVideo() API for generating videos from TypeScript scenes.
best_for: Programmatic, server-side video generation from templates
license_notes: MIT (copyright notice still names motion-canvas). Repository moved from redotvideo to midrender.
install_risk: Medium. Sends anonymous PostHog telemetry unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true.
reason: Agent-friendly headless rendering; turn telemetry off.

name: Manim Community
one_line: Python library for precise mathematical and diagram animation, rendered straight to video files.
best_for: Technical explainers, equations, graphs
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low-medium. Python package with Cairo/Pango system deps; LaTeX optional for maths text.
reason: Superb for diagrams, but a Python toolchain rather than browser-native.

name: p5.js
one_line: Friendly creative-coding library for canvas and WebGL sketches in the browser.
best_for: Generative backgrounds, particle fields, playful sketches
license_notes: LGPL-2.1 (per GitHub licence API, license.txt). Using the unmodified library in a page is fine; modified library files must stay LGPL.
install_risk: Low. Single JS file or npm package.
reason: Huge community and examples; easy for Opus to drive with a time-based draw.

name: PixiJS
one_line: Fast 2D renderer on WebGL/WebGPU with sprites, filters, text and masks.
best_for: Dense 2D scenes, sprite-heavy motion, filter effects
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Mature and fast; drive with your own clock for deterministic capture.

name: Theatre.js
one_line: Keyframe sequencing library with a visual studio for tuning animations of three.js or DOM.
best_for: Hand-tuning camera and keyframe curves on top of code
license_notes: Core is Apache-2.0, but the studio package (theatre/studio) is AGPL-3.0.
install_risk: Low. npm packages.
reason: Useful idea, but last push Aug 2024 and AGPL studio.

name: GSAP
one_line: Timeline animation library with plugins for text splitting, morphing and motion paths, now free.
best_for: Choreographing HTML/SVG/canvas scenes on a single seekable timeline
license_notes: Webflow's standard no-charge licence, not open source. Free including formerly paid plugins, but prohibited inside no-code visual animation builders that compete with Webflow; Webflow may amend terms; no GitHub LICENSE file.
install_risk: Low. npm or vendored file.
reason: Industry default and fine for making films; just do not build a competing visual builder on it.

name: Motion
one_line: Animation library for React and vanilla JS with springs, gestures, layout and scroll animation.
best_for: UI and website motion; React-based scenes
license_notes: MIT. Motion+ (examples, extra tooling) is a separate paid product.
install_risk: Low. npm. Its optional `npx motion-ai` installer sets up MCP servers for agents.
reason: Great for UI; for frame capture you must drive time manually.

name: anime.js
one_line: Lightweight engine for CSS, SVG, DOM and object animation with seekable timelines.
best_for: A permissive, small alternative to GSAP
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Permissive, compact, seekable.

name: lottie-web
one_line: Plays After Effects animations exported as Lottie JSON in SVG, canvas or HTML.
best_for: Dropping designer-made vector animations into a code film
license_notes: MIT. Authoring usually needs After Effects (paid) or another Lottie editor.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Reliable playback with goToAndStop seeking; repo quiet since Sept 2025.

name: Rive web runtime
one_line: WebAssembly/JS runtime that plays interactive Rive state-machine animations on canvas.
best_for: Reusing Rive-authored characters and UI animations
license_notes: Runtime MIT (C++ core rive-app/rive-runtime also MIT). Authoring .riv files happens in the Rive editor, a hosted app.
install_risk: Low. npm package with WASM binary.
reason: Runtime is open; content creation depends on the Rive editor.

name: Paper.js
one_line: Vector-graphics scripting on canvas with paths, boolean ops and a scene graph.
best_for: Path manipulation, line drawing and generative vector shapes
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Capable, but last push July 2024.

name: Two.js
one_line: Renderer-agnostic 2D drawing API that outputs to SVG, canvas or WebGL.
best_for: Flat vector motion that can switch between SVG and canvas
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Simple, maintained, permissive.

name: D3
one_line: Data-driven toolkit for scales, shapes, layouts and transitions in SVG or canvas.
best_for: Animated charts and data stories in launch films
license_notes: ISC (permissive).
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: The standard for data visuals; use its scales/shapes and drive time yourself.

name: GL Transitions
one_line: Open collection of GLSL shader transitions with a common uniform interface.
best_for: Shader wipes and morphs between scenes
license_notes: Collection MIT; each transition declares its own author and licence in a header comment, so check per file.
install_risk: Low. Plain GLSL files.
reason: Drop-in transitions that are trivially deterministic.

name: three.js
one_line: The standard JavaScript 3D library for WebGL and WebGPU scenes, materials and post-processing.
best_for: Product hero shots, 3D type, particle worlds
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package or ES modules.
reason: Huge ecosystem; Opus writes it fluently.

name: OGL
one_line: Minimal WebGL library with a three.js-like API at a fraction of the size.
best_for: Lean shader-driven scenes
license_notes: Unlicense (public-domain dedication), per README and package.json; GitHub detects no LICENSE file.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Nice and small, but last push April 2025.

name: regl
one_line: Functional, stateless wrapper around WebGL for writing draw commands.
best_for: Custom shader pipelines and GPU particle systems
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Powerful but low-level; more code for the agent to get right.

name: TWGL
one_line: Tiny helper that removes WebGL boilerplate for buffers, programs and textures.
best_for: Full-screen shader pieces with minimal setup
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Handy for shader-only pieces; low-level.

name: Zdog
one_line: Pseudo-3D engine drawing flat, rounded shapes to canvas or SVG.
best_for: Cute, flat 3D icons and mascots
license_notes: MIT per README and package.json; there is no LICENSE file in the repo.
install_risk: Low. Single JS file.
reason: Charming style; unmaintained since July 2023.

name: Tone.js
one_line: Web Audio framework with synths, effects, transport and offline rendering to a buffer.
best_for: Composing a score or SFX in code and rendering it offline to WAV
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Low. npm package.
reason: Lets the agent write music in the same codebase as the picture.

name: ZzFX
one_line: Tiny parameterised sound-effect generator for blips, whooshes and hits.
best_for: Quick UI sounds without sample licensing
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Very low. Single small JS file.
reason: Zero-licence-risk SFX in a few bytes.

name: FFmpeg
one_line: The universal command-line toolkit for encoding, muxing, filtering and loudness measurement.
best_for: Final encode, audio mux, loudness normalisation, GIFs
license_notes: LGPL-2.1+ by default; builds with --enable-gpl (most libx264 builds) are GPL-2.0+. Fine for running as a tool; matters only if you redistribute binaries.

name: Mediabunny
one_line: Pure TypeScript toolkit to read, write and convert MP4/WebM/audio in the browser via WebCodecs.
best_for: Encoding frames to MP4 inside the page, no ffmpeg round-trip
license_notes: MPL-2.0: usable in closed-source work; changes to its own files must stay MPL.
install_risk: Low. npm package, no native code.
reason: Fast in-browser encode path; actively maintained.

name: Playwright
one_line: Browser automation for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, used to step and screenshot frames.
best_for: Driving headless Chromium frame by frame
license_notes: Apache-2.0.

reason: The capture backbone most skills here rely on.

name: Puppeteer
one_line: Node API for controlling Chrome or Firefox, including screenshots and screencasts.
best_for: Chrome-only capture scripts and existing Puppeteer code
license_notes: Apache-2.0.
install_risk: Medium-low. Install downloads Chrome for Testing.
reason: Equivalent to Playwright for Chrome; pick one.

name: CCapture.js
one_line: Hooks requestAnimationFrame and timers to capture canvas animations at a fixed frame rate.
best_for: Capturing legacy canvas sketches that use real-time loops
license_notes: MIT.

name: Google Fonts
one_line: Source repository of every Google Fonts family, each folder carrying its own licence file.
best_for: Free, embeddable brand-quality typefaces

name: Fontsource
one_line: Open-source fonts packaged as versioned npm modules for self-hosting.
best_for: Pinning exact font versions in a render project
license_notes: Packaging code is MIT; each font keeps its own licence (mostly OFL).

reason: Makes renders reproducible offline.

name: opentype.js
one_line: Parses and writes OpenType fonts, exposing glyph outlines as paths.
best_for: Kinetic typography: per-glyph paths, outlines, morphs

name: Lucide

best_for: UI icons in product demos
license_notes: ISC; icons inherited from Feather are MIT. Both permissive.

name: Heroicons
one_line: Outline and solid SVG icons from the Tailwind CSS team.
best_for: Simple UI icons matching Tailwind products
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Very low. SVG files.

name: Phosphor Icons

license_notes: MIT (core assets repo; the homepage repo, 7.6k stars, is also MIT).
install_risk: Very low. SVG files or npm.
reason: Weight variants are great for animated emphasis.

name: Tabler Icons

best_for: Broad icon coverage for dashboards and diagrams
license_notes: MIT.
install_risk: Very low. SVG files or npm.
reason: Largest permissive set here.

name: Simple Icons
one_line: SVG logos for thousands of brands with their official colours.

reason: Handy, but trademark law, not copyright, is the real constraint.

name: Awesome Motion Design Agent Skills
one_line: Curated motion-design stack for agents plus five installable skills, with dated repo metadata.
best_for: Discovering GSAP/Motion/Remotion/Lottie/Rive resources
license_notes: CC0 for the list; linked projects keep their own licences.

name: Awesome Claude Video Skills
one_line: Large index of open-source video-making skills and toolkits for Claude Code, Codex and others.
best_for: Finding niche video skills beyond this map
license_notes: List text CC0; quoted repo names/descriptions belong to their authors; each project has its own licence.

reason: Broadest index found; updated 2026-10-11.

name: Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos
one_line: Gallery of widely shared Opus 5.5 videos with the prompts behind them.
best_for: Prompt inspiration and reference quality bar
license_notes: MIT for the list; the videos and prompts quoted belong to their creators.

reason: Best prompt-to-result reference set (4k+ stars).

name: PDoomVideo
one_line: Full source of a well-known Opus 5.5 music video, including the first-generation version.
best_for: Studying how a viral code-rendered music video is structured
license_notes: No LICENSE file (package.json says ISC, which is not a repo licence grant on its own). Song is third-party. Treat as read-only.
